generated_test_cases.title: Verify get_db returns a session instance
generated_test_cases.description: Ensure that calling get_db returns a valid SQLAlchemy session object connected to the test database.
expected_results: A non-null session object is returned
Session is bound to the test database

generated_test_cases.title: Handle missing database URL
generated_test_cases.description: Test get_db behavior when DATABASE_URL environment variable is not set.
expected_results: Raises a ValueError with message indicating missing DATABASE_URL

generated_test_cases.title: Application starts with correct config
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that the main application initializes without errors and loads configuration.
expected_results: Application starts and logs initialization success

generated_test_cases.title: Application fails on missing config file
generated_test_cases.description: Ensure that the application raises an error if required configuration file is missing.
expected_results: Application exits with error code and logs missing config

generated_test_cases.title: Create item missing name field
generated_test_cases.description: Attempt to create an item without the required 'name' field and expect validation failure.
steps: Send POST request to /items/ with JSON body {"description": "Missing name"}.
expected_results: Response status code is 422 (Unprocessable Entity) with validation error indicating missing 'name'.

generated_test_cases.title: Delete non‑existent item
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that deleting an item that does not exist returns a 404 error.
steps: Send DELETE request to /items/9999 where 9999 is an ID not present in the database.
expected_results: Response status code is 404 as defined in exception_status_mappings.

generated_test_cases.title: Delete existing item successfully
generated_test_cases.description: Ensure that deleting an existing item returns a 204 status and removes the record.
steps: Create an item via POST /items/ with valid data.
Query the database for the item.
expected_results: DELETE response status code is 204.
The item is no longer present in the database.

generated_test_cases.title: Create item with maximum field lengths
generated_test_cases.description: Test boundary conditions by providing maximum allowed lengths for name and description.
steps: Construct a JSON payload where 'name' and 'description' are at their maximum length limits.
Send POST request to /items/ with this payload.
expected_results: Response status code is 201 and the item is created successfully without truncation.

generated_test_cases.title: Delete non-db item positive
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that deleting an item that does not exist returns 204 and no error.
expected_results: Response status is 204
Database unchanged

generated_test_cases.title: Delete non-db item negative
generated_test_cases.description: Attempt to delete a non-existing item and ensure system handles gracefully.
expected_results: Response status is 204
No error thrown

generated_test_cases.title: Delete item with not-not-db-item positive
generated_test_cases.description: Verify deletion when item exists (not(not db_item))
expected_results: Response status is 204
Item removed from database

generated_test_cases.title: Get item function positive
generated_test_cases.description: Ensure get_item function returns correct item data
expected_results: Response status is 200
Response body matches created item

generated_test_cases.title: Delete item when database flag is false (not (not db_item))
generated_test_cases.description: Verify that when the system indicates an item exists but the deletion condition fails, the API still returns 404.
steps: Mock database to return a valid item for ID 1234 but set internal flag such that delete condition is negated.
expected_results: API responds with 404 Not Found status code.
Response body contains error message indicating deletion condition not met.
